title: Path Sum II
summary: Find all paths from the tree's root to its leaf nodes where the sum of node values equals the target sum.
statement: Find all paths from the tree's root to its leaf nodes where the sum of node values equals the target sum. Each path must be listed with node values, not node references. A leaf node is defined as a node with no children.
constraints: Return every root-to-leaf path whose values sum to target_sum. Preserve value order within a path; outer path order is unrestricted.
Two different leaf paths may have identical values; include both. A leaf has no left or right child.

hints: Track the complete current root-to-node path and its sum.
Only a leaf may complete a qualifying path; negative values mean partial sums cannot safely prune branches.
On entering a node, append its value and add it to the sum. Copy a matching leaf path. After its children, remove the node and subtract its value.
Use explicit enter/leave frames to reproduce recursion safely for a 5000-node chain.
editorial: Backtracking maintains one path and running sum. Entering a node extends them; leaving restores their prior state. Copy a matching path only at a leaf. Explicit enter/leave frames express recursive depth-first traversal without depending on Python's recursion limit. Duplicate value sequences from different leaves remain separate answers. With S total values in returned paths, time is O(n+S), while working frames and path use O(h) storage. The independent oracle enumerates leaf position keys and reconstructs each ancestor sequence.
